long-covid.title: [Intersection of gender, working conditions, and caregiving burden in post-COVID-19 syndrome: A cross-sectional mixed-methods study among healthcare workers].
long-covid.authors: Antonietti, Laura, Straw, Cecilia, Riveiro, Manuel, Martínez, María José et al.
long-covid.excerpt: Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) among healthcare personnel impacts quality of life and work performance negatively, and is associated with gender and work conditions. The study aimed to characterize PCS in healthcare personnel and explore their perceptions regarding gender conditions, work, and caregiving burden.

long-covid.title: [An insight into the long/post COVID care situation in Germany-a rapid scoping review].
long-covid.authors: Ebster, Marlene, Gscheidle, Sonja, Lange, Saskia, Weijburg, Thomas et al.
long-covid.excerpt: Long/post COVID and related conditions such as myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome, postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome and post-vaccination syndrome are associated with persistent functional impairments and are met with care structures in Germany that are difficult to navigate. The rapid scoping review offers an insight into care structures, capacities, access, care pathways and gaps in care...

long-covid.title: Potential Physiological Convergence Between GLP-1 Receptor Signaling and Hepatocyte TAZ in Metabolic Liver Disease: From Metabolic Homeostasis to Fibrotic Remodeling.
long-covid.excerpt: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) progresses when nutrient excess, insulin resistance, adipose dysfunction, and hepatocellular stress overwhelm hepatic adaptation. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) improve weight, glycemic control, and steatohepatitis, and semaglutide has demonstrated histological improvement in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH).

long-covid.title: Dysregulated complement activation in COVID-19: The Role of Soluble Complement Inhibitors.
long-covid.authors: van der Meulen, Stef, Wang, Haiyu, Nugteren, Saskia, Ponchel, Frederique et al.
long-covid.excerpt: In viral infections, complement activation can contribute to viral clearance, but excessive activation, as observed in severe COVID-19, may drive immunopathology. While much is known about complement-activating factors in COVID-19, insight into the role of endogenous complement inhibitors remains limited.

pots.title: Post-translational modifications in the insoluble fraction of platelet-poor plasma distinguish pre-COVID-19 Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome, Long COVID, and Long COVID-POTS: a preliminary study.

pots.excerpt: Exogenous testosterone has been previously reported to have given clinical improvement in symptoms of postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) in reported cases of transgender patients during their transition from female to male. Herein is presented two case reports of cisgender heterosexual female patients with POTS who have used testosterone for the management of concurrent gynecologic problems, but who...

pots.title: Evidence of autoimmune etiology in children with small fiber neuropathy.
pots.authors: Rook, Morgan, Perry, Fredrick, Zaheer, Aalif, Safder, Shaista et al.
pots.excerpt: Small fiber neuropathy (SFN) is becoming increasingly recognized as a cause of autonomic dysfunction, sensory disturbances, and neuropathic pain. While SFN was previously considered predominantly idiopathic, cases of autoimmune SFN are now well described in adults but remain underexplored in children.

mcas.title: Topical Remibrutinib Attenuates LL37-Induced Rosacea-Like Dermatitis by Inhibiting BTK Activation, NF-κB Signaling and Mast Cell Activation.
mcas.authors: Li, Wangchao, Fan, Huiping, Liu, Hua, Ma, Qingsong et al.
mcas.excerpt: Rosacea is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder in which LL37-driven mast cell activation contributes to cutaneous inflammation. Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) is a key regulator of canonical IgE-dependent mast cell responses; however, its role in LL37-induced, IgE-independent mast cell activation remains unclear.

mcas.title: Thiophene-Benzimidazole Conjugates Attenuate IL-33-induced Inflammation in Human Mast Cell Line and in ex vivo Human Skin Organ Cultures.
mcas.authors: Gvirtz, Raanan, Kahremany, Shirin, Trifonov, Lena, Weintraub, Sagiv et al.
mcas.excerpt: Aberrant Interleukin-33 (IL-33) activation is associated with numerous dermatological inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, such as atopic dermatitis, lupus, vitiligo and psoriasis. Thus, the inhibition of this pathway may provide therapeutic options in multiple pathologies.

mcas.title: Phenotyping Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome: Clinical and Mechanistic Evidence, Candidate Biomarkers, and Implications for Management.
mcas.authors: Qiao, Pengfei, Tian, Zhentao, He, Zhen
mcas.excerpt: Interstitial cystitis and bladder pain syndrome are clinically overlapping conditions that should be distinguished according to Hunner lesion status. IC with Hunner lesions is a distinct inflammatory bladder disease characterized by urothelial denudation, lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, adaptive immune activation, and progressive structural impairment.

mcas.title: Noninvasive urinary biomarkers 3-bromotyrosine and leukotriene E4 in assessing asthma control and flare-up in children: a case-control study.
mcas.authors: Yadav, Krishna Kumar, Gupta, Nitesh R, Yadav, Sunita, Kulshrestha, Manish Raj et al.
mcas.excerpt: To assess urinary biomarkers 3-bromotyrosine and leukotriene E4 (LTE4) levels in children with asthma and their association with asthma control and flare-up. This was a prospective study which applied a case-control design with 2:1 ratio.

mcas.title: Genetically engineering mast cells as effectors for targeted cancer cell cytotoxicity.
mcas.authors: Han, Xiao, Wen, Di, Fu, Ruxing, Soto, Jennifer et al.
mcas.excerpt: Type-I hypersensitivity is a mast cell-mediated degranulation process induced by IgE-antigen recognition. Inspired by this highly specific mechanism, we developed a new cell therapy platform by genetically engineering mouse mast cell line MC/9 to overexpress the cytotoxic proteins perforin and granzyme B (PG-MCs) via lentiviral transduction.

mcas.title: CD300f acts as an inducible inhibitory checkpoint that limits mast cell activation by suppressing MITF-dependent activation.
mcas.authors: Song, Lihong, Ollé, Laia, Zhang, Zeng, Lago, Natalia et al.
mcas.excerpt: Mast cells (MCs) are key regulators of cutaneous immune responses and play a central role in allergic and non-IgE-mediated skin inflammation by activating the Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 (MRGPRX2). The inhibitory receptor CD300f has been shown to modulate MC activation, but its role in regulating MRGPRX2-dependent signaling remains unclear.

mcas.title: A Review: Mast Cells as Targets for Glucocorticoid Action.
mcas.authors: Atum, Daniel, Ogwal, Jimmy Odongo, Obeny, Abel
mcas.excerpt: This review aims to summarize the established and potential targets of glucocorticoids (GCs) on mast cells, which are implicated in the pathophysiology of various allergic and inflammatory diseases including asthma, allergic rhinitis, and atopic dermatitis. We sought to answer the following questions: (1) How do glucocorticoids inhibit the release of mediators from mast cells?

mcas.title: Hsp90 inhibitor 17-AAG reduces skin inflammation and inhibits NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome activation in DNCB-induced mice and TNF-α/IFN-γ-induced keratinocytes.
mcas.excerpt: Atopic dermatitis (AD) represents the most common inflammatory skin condition with a high burden of disease persistence and relapse. In this study, we aimed to investigate the role of 17-AAG, a Hsp90 inhibitor, in inhibiting skin inflammation in AD and its effect on nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB)/NOD-like receptor thermal protein domain associated protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome pathway.

Here, we address this challenge using melamine cyanurate (MCA), whose supramolecular...

mcas.title: Mast cell activation syndromes in clinical practice: diagnostic challenges, phenotypes, and real-life management.
mcas.authors: Katran, Zeynep Yegin, Argın, Özge, Erdem, Simge, Bulut, İsmet
mcas.excerpt: Mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) is characterized by recurrent, systemic episodes of mast cell mediator release, often resembling anaphylaxis and involving multiple organ systems. To describe clinical, laboratory, and therapeutic characteristics of patients with non-clonal mast cell activation syndromes in a real-life cohort.

mcas.title: Outcome selection and reporting transparency in ClinicalTrials.gov-registered chronic spontaneous urticaria trials: a registry-publication linkage study.
mcas.authors: Liu, Yannan, Gao, Ruhong, Peng, Yongjun, Ma, Wenli et al.
mcas.excerpt: Chronic spontaneous urticaria/chronic idiopathic urticaria (CSU/CIU) trials increasingly evaluate biologics and targeted mast-cell therapies. Whether ClinicalTrials.gov-registered trials consistently capture patient-centred outcomes and disseminate results in a timely and linkable manner remains uncertain.

mcas.excerpt: Asthma is a chronic allergic airway inflammation that requires ongoing therapeutic intervention and reduces the patient's quality of life. Therefore, safe and efficacious drugs for the treatment of asthma are urgently needed.

mcas.excerpt: Microscopic colitis (MC) is an inflammatory bowel disease characterized by chronic watery diarrhea. Although barrier dysfunction and immune activation are implicated, underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

mcas.title: Cell-intrinsic steroidogenesis regulates mast cell function.
mcas.authors: Pramanik, Jhuma, Zhao, Qiuchen, Chakraborty, Soura, Yamashita-Kanemaru, Yumi et al.
mcas.excerpt: Steroid hormones are well-known regulators of mast cell function, but whether mast cells themselves produce steroids de novo and influences their effector function has remained unknown. Here, we show that mast cells constitutively express the steroidogenic enzyme cytochrome P450 family 11 subfamily A member 1 (Cyp11a1) and produce pregnenolone.
